summary: Former Forest Service Devil Mountain tower, moved by Chinook to Jicarilla Apache land in 1996; BIA-run and listed standing; no public access found.

facts.design: Forest Service CL 100 series metal cab with flat metal roof and catwalk on a steel tower (register); the Devil Mountain entry gives different dimensions

staffing.status: in active service by the BIA (register; undated)

access.note: On Jicarilla Apache land and run by the BIA. I found no public visiting rules.

events.note: Built as Devil Mountain Lookout on the San Juan National Forest, Colorado, to take over duties from Chimney Rock
Cultural resource survey for relocating the Tecolote Mesa fire tower on Jicarilla Apache lands
Moved in three trips by a Nevada Army National Guard Chinook (register). The Devil Mountain entry says it was sold to the Jicarilla Apache Nation in the 1990s

evidence.supports: Built by the Forest Service as Devil Mountain Lookout on the San Juan National Forest, Colorado
evidence.quote: Atole Lookout was constructed by the U.S. Forest Service as Devil Mountain Lookout on the San Juan National Forest in southwestern Colorado.

evidence.supports: Devil Mountain tower built 1955 to take over duties from Chimney Rock; 30 ft tower and 13 by 13 ft cab
evidence.quote: This 30' steel tower with 13'x13' steel cab was built in 1955 to take over lookout duties from Chimney Rock.

evidence.supports: Surplus tower claimed by BIA; 1996 Chinook move in three trips
evidence.quote: Declared surplus, the Bureau of Indian Affairs claimed it and in 1996 a twin rotor Chinook helicopter from the Nevada Army National Guard moved the fire tower in three trips.

evidence.supports: Sold to the Jicarilla Apache Nation in the 1990s, moved, and called Atole
evidence.quote: In the 1990s it was sold to the Jicarilla Apache Nation in New Mexico and moved to a location on their lands, where it is called Atole.

evidence.supports: Tecolote Mesa site chosen to give detection over 131,000 acres of land the tribe bought
evidence.quote: A site on Tecolote Mesa was selected to provide detection on 131,000 acres of additional land purchased by the tribe.

evidence.supports: Register's dimensions: 14 by 14 ft cab, CL 100 series design, 40 ft steel tower
evidence.quote: The 14' x 14' metal cab with corrugated flat metal roof and catwalk is of the Forest Service CL 100 series design and mounted on a 40' steel tower.

evidence.supports: Lookout is in active service by the BIA
evidence.quote: This primary lookout is in active service by the BIA.

notes_for_editor: Identity is settled: the Devil Mountain site entry says the tower became Atole, and the register describes the same Forest Service design. Unresolved: (1) Dimensions differ: register 14x14 ft cab on 40 ft tower; Devil Mountain entry 13x13 ft cab on 30 ft tower. Neither source says the tower was rebuilt, so no height_m is recorded. (2) Ownership: register says BIA claimed the surplus tower; Devil Mountain entry says it was sold to the Jicarilla Apache Nation. (3) Location: register coordinates (36.853623, -106.774975) and the FFLA list (36.77535, -106.74914) are about 9 km apart; the story follows the register, which is the record's point. A site check or tribal source would settle it. (4) The 1996 move date comes from the register alone; the Devil Mountain entry gives only 'the 1990s'. (5) Access: no public rules found; restricted is an inference from tribal land and BIA service. No notable fires found. The record's material 'steel' is supported by the register's steel tower.
